candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — activity/rest balance, energy conservation, symptom management, and maintenance of functional comfort.
candidate.educational_objective: Teach balanced energy conservation for cancer-related fatigue by combining prioritization and short planned rest with individualized safe activity rather than complete inactivity or indiscriminate overexertion.

options.A: Plan short rest periods and prioritize the activities that matter most, but balance rest with an individualized level of physical activity rather than remaining completely inactive.
options.B: Complete bed rest is the preferred fatigue-management strategy because physical activity reliably worsens cancer-related fatigue.
options.C: Ignore fatigue when planning the day and complete all usual activities at the same pace regardless of symptoms.
options.D: Avoid discussing activity with the healthcare team because fatigue-management strategies do not need to be individualized.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. NCI recommends planned rest, prioritizing the most important activities, and doing activities when energy is highest. NCI also supports individualized physical activity and exercise because activity can reduce cancer-related fatigue and help maintain function; complete inactivity is not the general goal. B is incorrect because routine complete bed rest can promote deconditioning and is not NCI's recommended fatigue strategy. C is incorrect because pacing and prioritization are appropriate when fatigue interferes with function. D is incorrect because activity should be individualized to the client's condition, treatment, safety, and functional ability.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Cancer-related fatigue management includes planned rest, prioritization and scheduling of important activities, plus individualized physical activity/exercise rather than complete inactivity.
candidate.source_document_title: Fatigue and Cancer; Fatigue (PDQ®) — Health Professional Version; Physical Activity and Cancer Fact Sheet
candidate.source_locator: Fatigue and Cancer — management bullets under 'Rest and sleep' and 'Exercise and physical activity'; Fatigue PDQ — 'Patient Education' and exercise evidence sections, including scheduling important activities during times of least fatigue and encouraging planned exercise within individual limitations; Physical Activity and Cancer Fact Sheet — section 'Is physical activity beneficial for cancer survivors?'.
candidate.source_organization: National Cancer Institute (NCI), National Institutes of Health
candidate.stem: A client with cancer-related fatigue says, 'I think I should stay in bed all day so I do not waste any energy.' Which response by the nurse is most appropriate?
